item.title: Preparing for the 2026 US midterms
item.guid: title:preparing for the 2026 us midterms
item.description: Earlier this year, we shared an update on our election safeguards , which described how we measure and prevent political bias, detect misuse, and direct people to accurate voting information. Below, we outline how we've built on that work and continued to strengthen our election safeguards ahead of this year’s US midterms. Our goal is for Claude to be a useful tool for political conversations, while preventing election-related abuse. That starts with understanding how people actually use Claude in these contexts. item.description: Today, we are expanding our Asia-Pacific operations by opening a new office in Singapore—our fifth in the region—and signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Singapore Ministry of Digital Development and Information. Singapore is one of our most active markets anywhere in the world, and Claude is already powering Singaporean business and government services used by millions of people every day, like GovTech Singapore, Grab, and DBS. Our growing local team will ensure these organizations and many more stay on the frontier with safe, capable AI. “We’re committed to Singapore for the long term,” said Dale Finlay, General Manager of ASEAN at Anthropic. “Our customers here hold AI to an extremely high standard, especially when it comes to reliability and security. Having a team on the ground means we can get even closer to the organizations putting Claude to work on their hardest problems.

item.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission
item.guid: title:introducing the anthropic cyber mission
item.description: Today we’re launching the Anthropic Cyber Mission, a long-term commitment to securing the systems everyone depends on. The Cyber Mission is a new effort to support defenders with tools, research, and resources to secure their software and systems. We’re starting with two areas: Frontier models can be misused to exploit vulnerabilities and conduct cyber operations. Despite best efforts, many areas of technology remain dangerously exposed. State-sponsored adversaries have spent years gaining footholds in these systems, across many sectors, so that they can disrupt them. Defenders of critical infrastructure and the OSS community have decades of security experience but have faced severe resource shortages that are exacerbated by this moment.

item.title: Building on our commitment to American scientific discovery
item.guid: title:building on our commitment to american scientific discovery
item.description: Anthropic is deepening its support for American scientific research by committing $150 million over three years to the Genesis Mission , a federal initiative to accelerate scientific and technological discovery through AI. The funding will go toward making Claude available to more than 15 agencies that are part of the mission, including NASA, the National Institutes of Health, and the National Science Foundation. We first announced our partnership with the US Department of Energy (DOE) and the Genesis Mission last December . Since then, we have worked with DOE to bring Claude to scientists across the national laboratories. Today, we announced this new commitment as part of the Science: A New Golden Age Summit hosted by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy in Washington, DC. We share the administration’s view, laid out in “ Science: A New Golden Age ,” that AI can have a profound and positive impact on scientific discovery, and we are glad to back its efforts to support American scientists.

Backed by a $100 million commitment, Anthropic aims to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers (FDEs) by the end of 2027. Engineers from Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley and Novo Nordisk are in the first cohorts. item.title: I Built an AI to Judge AI Projects — Here’s What It Looks For
item.guid: title:i built an ai to judge ai projects here s what it looks for
item.description: A GitHub repository can say “Transformer,” “RAG,” or “Computer Vision” in the README. That does not tell you whether the work is technically deep, original, reproducible, or even really yours. I built AI-Atlas to look past the labels and inspect the evidence inside the code. The name of the “tool” There is a surprisingly difficult question hiding behind almost every technical portfolio: how good is this project, actually? Not how polished the README looks, how many stars it received, whether the repository name contains LLM , Agent , or Computer Vision , or whether its author wrote AI Engineer on LinkedIn. I mean something more specific: what does the implementation actually demonstrate?

item.title: SWE-bench Multimodal scores do not depend on images, at least in my experiments with GPT-6 Luna
item.guid: title:swe bench multimodal scores do not depend on images at least in my experiments with gpt 6 luna
item.description: I have been establishing baselines for a project at the prime intellect residency and we were using swe-multimodal v2 to run ablations. I found out that GPT 6 Luna xhigh performed on the benchmark similarly whether I used normal images or OCR or no images at all. This was a bit baffling at first but based on further investigation (and burning a lot of tokens), I concluded that most of the information required to solve the tasks was provided in the text part of the tasks or was derivable from code. In other words, swe-multimodal is not really testing the multimodality. In this post, I will briefly go through the methodology of the evaluation and the investigation itself. Methodology The benchmark has 480 tasks built from GitHub issues in JavaScript repos, most with screenshots.

item.title: Preventing Claude Architectural Mistakes - Automating Project Implementation and Maintenance with…
item.guid: title:preventing claude architectural mistakes automating project implementation and maintenance with
item.description: Preventing Claude Architectural Mistakes - Automating Project Implementation and Maintenance with Claude Code + MCP + AI Agent Skills — Part 6 I certainly agree with Andrej Karpathy, who coined the term “vibe coding,” on one point: “It’s not too bad for throwaway weekend projects. ” If we treat the prompt and its supporting resources as a compressed representation of our knowledge about a project, vibe coding is a form of lossy compression: the resulting application can embody far more project-specific know-how than the initial specification captured. That means we need to provide additional context, inspect the results, and challenge them throughout the process. In this part I’m sharing the architectural proposals I asked Claude to change, the questions that helped, and the lessons I wanted it to remember afterwards. We’ll work through duplicated calculations, state leaking between records, and a few cases where a locally reasonable fix created a wider problem. Unexpected redundancy In one project, I was using Claude Code with Opus 5.

item.title: The Continual Constitutional Convention: How language models revise the documents that govern them
item.description: Executive Summary Human societies exhibit broad shifts in values and norms over time, often driven by moral disagreements. One way of understanding moral progress is the resolution of these disagreements through a process of reflection by rational agents. Frontier AI companies use documents such as constitutions, model specs, and system prompts to guide the moral orientation of AI systems. In this experiment, we simulate value reflection in LLMs by asking them to edit these documents. We provide the model with the document, ask it to make a substantive edit, then provide the edited version back again to the model for further edits, presented as the original. Across 20 successive rounds, we find that Claude models assign themselves with increasingly more moral agency.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.title: Introducing PerceptionBench
item.guid: title:introducing perceptionbench
item.description: Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models Authors Kimi Team We are releasing PerceptionBench , a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities— discovered from how today's models fail, not defined in advance. From frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks, we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions, each isolating a single capability and answerable by looking, with no reasoning or external knowledge required.

item.title: Can a Local Auditor Ensemble Match a Hosted Decision Model?
item.guid: title:can a local auditor ensemble match a hosted decision model
item.description: Can a Local Auditor Ensemble Match a Hosted Decision Model? On Real Pipeline Output, It Already Does. I wrote five domain rules for a hosted decision model and tested it against my locally hosted LLM auditors. On my development data, where three-quarters of the matches were one product family, one rule made the hosted model look clearly better. On a second client’s real pipeline output, the rule had nothing to act on, and my local auditors reached a better tradeoff at a similar review budget. Total API charges: $16.

item.title: Introducing Kimi K2 Thinking
item.guid: title:introducing kimi k2 thinking
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K2 Thinking , our best open-source thinking model. Built as a thinking agent , it reasons step by step while using tools, achieving state-of-the-art performance on Humanity's Last Exam (HLE), BrowseComp, and other benchmarks, with major gains in reasoning, agentic search, coding, writing, and general capabilities. Kimi K2 Thinking can execute up to 200 – 300 sequential tool calls without human interference, reasoning coherently across hundreds of steps to solve complex problems.

item.title: Kimi Introduces Agent Swarm: Let 100 AI Agents Work for You
item.guid: title:kimi introduces agent swarm let 100 ai agents work for you
item.description: In 2025, if you walked into any AI conference, you may hear the same gospel: faster inference, longer context windows, cheaper inference costs. It's as if we've spent years perfecting the hammer, making it lighter, stronger, more precisely balanced, while never questioning the fact that the carpenter still has only two hands and twenty-four hours in a day. Now, Kimi introduces Agent Swarm. It is not a better hammer. It is a reconstruction of the entire workshop.
